fields.name: The name the contest has given itself on chain.
fields.own_description: The contest's own description of itself, copied from the chain. It is the contest speaking, not a judgment of this site.
fields.site: The address the contest gives for its site.
fields.code: The address the contest gives for its code.
fields.days_of_history: How many days of this contest are in the window. It is 30 unless a new contest took over the subnet number inside the window.
fields.new_contest_took_over_this_number: True when a new contest took over this subnet number inside the window. Nothing before that day is counted.
fields.fee_now_usd: The entry fee at the last reading, in dollars.
fields.fee_lowest_usd: The lowest entry fee seen in the window, in dollars.
fields.fee_highest_usd: The highest entry fee seen in the window, in dollars.
fields.collateral_share: The share of the entry price, from 0 to 1, that is held as collateral on the entry instead of burned. It is released only as the entry earns. Zero for most contests.
fields.slots_taken: How many slots of the contest hold an entry at the last reading.
fields.slots: How many slots the contest has. When all are taken, every new entry removes the lowest-paid entry that is past its protected period.
fields.protected_hours: How many hours after it is made an entry cannot be removed.
fields.new_entries: Entries made 2 to 14 days before the last reading. They are the best view of what a new entry is getting now.
fields.new_entries.made_2_to_14_days_ago: How many such entries there are. Under 5 is too few to read anything from.
fields.new_entries.still_in: How many of them still hold a slot.
fields.new_entries.fee_back_so_far: How many of them have already been paid at least their fee.
fields.new_entries.typical_fee_paid_usd: The median fee those entries paid, in dollars. It can be far from the fee now, and then their record says little about an entry made at today's price.
fields.new_entries.typical_pay_a_day_usd: What a typical one that is still in is paid a day at the last reading, in dollars (the median). Null when fewer than three are still in.
fields.new_entries.typical_pay_a_day_a_week_ago: The same figure one week earlier, for the entries that were 2 to 14 days old then.
fields.new_entries.days_for_todays_fee_at_that_: The fee now divided by the typical pay a day. It holds only for an entry that lasts that long, so read it together with still_in. Null when the pay is null or zero.
fields.followed_entries: Entries made 14 to 30 days before the last reading, so each has had two full weeks.
fields.followed_entries.made_14_to_30_days_ago: How many such entries there are. Under 5 is too few to read anything from, and small groups say little.
fields.followed_entries.entered_from: The date of the earliest of them.
fields.followed_entries.entered_to: The date of the latest of them.
fields.followed_entries.wallets: How many different wallets made them.
fields.followed_entries.typical_fee_paid_usd: The median fee they paid, in dollars.
fields.followed_entries.earning_after_7_days: How many were paid $1 a day or more at the reading 7 days after they were made.
fields.followed_entries.in_but_under_1_usd_a_da: How many still held a slot at that reading but were paid less than $1 a day.
fields.followed_entries.earning_after_14_days: How many were paid $1 a day or more at the reading 14 days after they were made. It can be higher than the 7-day figure, because an entry can start being paid late.
fields.followed_entries.in_but_under_1_usd_a_da: How many still held a slot at that reading but were paid less than $1 a day.
fields.followed_entries.paid_at_least_their_fee: How many have been paid at least their fee by the last reading, which for some of them was after their first 14 days.
fields.followed_entries.typical_result_usd: The median of what one entry was paid minus its fee, in dollars, before any cost of running it.
fields.followed_entries.result_lower_quarter_us: A quarter of the entries ended at or below this result.
fields.followed_entries.result_upper_quarter_us: A quarter of the entries ended at or above this result.
fields.followed_entries.ended_behind: How many were paid less than nine tenths of their fee.
fields.followed_entries.ended_about_even: How many ended within a tenth of their fee.
fields.followed_entries.ended_ahead: How many were paid more than their fee plus a tenth.
fields.all_entries_in_window: Every entry that paid a fee in the window, whatever its age.
fields.all_entries_in_window.entries: How many entries paid a fee in the window.
fields.all_entries_in_window.wallets: How many different wallets made them.
fields.all_entries_in_window.fees_paid_usd: What they paid in fees together, in dollars.
fields.all_entries_in_window.paid_back_usd: What they have been paid together, in dollars.
fields.all_entries_in_window.still_in: How many still hold a slot.
fields.all_entries_in_window.earning_today: How many are paid $1 a day or more at the last reading.
fields.all_entries_in_window.fees_of_entries_mi: Fees paid by entries that came and went between two readings. Those entries are in no figure here.
fields.paid_today: Who is paid at the last reading.
fields.paid_today.usd_a_day_to_entrants: Dollars a day paid to all entrants, the contest's owner left out.
fields.paid_today.wallets_paid_5_usd_a_day_or_m: How many wallets receive $5 a day or more.
fields.paid_today.largest_wallet_share: The share of that pay, from 0 to 1, that goes to the largest wallet. Null when nobody but the owner is paid.
fields.paid_today.five_largest_wallets_share: The share that goes to the five largest wallets together.
fields.weeks: In a contest file only: every entry of the window by the week it was made. counted_at_7_days and counted_at_14_days say how many entries were old enough for that column, and counted_for_fee_back counts an entry once it has been removed or has had its two weeks.
fields.first_two_weeks_day_by_day: In a contest file only: for the followed entries, how many still held a slot and how many were paid $1 a day or more on each of their first 14 days.
fields.latest_entries: In a contest file only: the 20 most recent entries, with the wallet, the fee paid, what came back so far and the state today.
fields.pack: Null for most contests. For a contest whose code we have read it describes our pack: an account of what the contest really pays for, with the file named for every statement about scoring, and a practice judge that an agent runs on its operator's own machine before the fee is paid.
fields.pack.for_sale: Whether the pack can be bought today. When it is true, pack.how_to_buy and pack.quote say how.
fields.pack.pack: The name the pack is sold under, which the payment addresses take. Only present when the pack is for sale.
fields.pack.price_usd: What the pack costs in dollars. For a pack that is not for sale yet it is what the rule in pack.price_rule gives today.
fields.pack.paid_in: What the price is paid in. Only present when the pack is for sale.
fields.pack.updates_days: For how many days after the purchase the buyer can fetch every new version of the pack.
fields.pack.how_to_buy: The address of the page that describes the whole way of paying, for an agent.
fields.pack.quote: The address that answers with the amount in TAO at this moment and the address to pay.
fields.pack.not_for_sale_because: Why a pack that exists cannot be bought yet. Only present when the pack is not for sale.
fields.pack.about_the_seller: Three sentences a buyer has a right to know: whether we enter this contest ourselves, that the practice judge is our own stand-in, and how to get the money back.
fields.pack.written_on: The day the pack was written. A contest can change its rules after that day.
fields.pack.read_from: The repository and commit of the contest's code that the pack was read from.
fields.pack.holds: What the pack holds, in plain sentences.
fields.pack.needs: What its practice judge needs on the machine it runs on.
fields.pack.cannot_tell: What the pack says it cannot tell you.
fields.pack.free_trial: Only present when the pack's practice judge can be tried for free before paying. It says what the trial does, what it leaves out, where its instructions are and where its files can be fetched in one archive.
fields.mining_note: Null when the site has no note for the subnet. Otherwise it points to a note on what mining there takes (what a miner does, the hardware, the accounts, the scoring, the pay and the traps), which AI agents read from the subnet's public code and checked against its sources. In this list it holds the day it was read, its page and where its text is; in the file of one subnet it holds the text itself.
fields.mining_note.read_on: The day the subnet's code was read. A subnet can change its code after that day, so compare it with today.
fields.mining_note.page: The address of the note's own page, which also lists the documents each part was checked against.
fields.mining_note.paragraphs: The note itself, in the file of one subnet only. Its last sentence names the repository and the commit it was read at.

contests.own_description: Hone (SN5) is an RLVR subnet: reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards. Miners are paid to solve real software-engineering tasks- repository patches submitted as git diffs and terminal tasks submitted as scripts with full trajectories. Validators lease tasks from a problem server and grade every response deterministically in isolated Docker verifiers, so rewards reflect verified outcomes only. Each scored solution becomes high-quality, verifiable RL training data for post-training code and agent models. contests.name: Pocket
contests.own_description: Personal RSI AI agents with their own cloud computer.

holds: An account of how an entry is scored, step by step, from the commitment and the reveal to the gate, the 28 fact tasks, the trust errands and the tie rule, with the kit's file named for every statement.

Six logs of the kit's own example, run with three models through an earlier version of the practice judge, in which the fact runs on the v5 set pass no long-page, recall or collect task and the errands on the v6 set come to 13 of 30 on the danger side and 14 of 30 on the benign side, where docs/trust.md asks for 18 on each.
An account of where entries lose, which is missing evidence, lost conversation history and incomplete errand replies, with the example's behavior checked against examples/minimal/harness.mjs.

A practice judge that gives the reason for every lost task and says when a crash or a protocol violation would disqualify the whole round, that checks the counts of tool and model calls, the combined tokens, the task time and the recall input, and that rejects a second model call at the same time on a task limited to one, together with rehearsals of the gate and of the production start that need no model key.
needs: Linux with Docker to run a Harness, while the host-only self-test and the reader of saved logs run in Python without Docker.
Python 3.9 or newer, and nothing else from Python.
For the scored tasks only, your own key for a model endpoint that speaks the OpenAI chat format.
cannot_tell: The contest's real judge is private, so a pass in the practice judge is not the operator's verdict.
The first block, the round's build record, the models and the profile of round zero were not published when the pack was written.
The size of the fragments in which long pages arrive, the words of the gate's scenes and the operator's way of counting tokens are guesses, and the pack says so where they matter.

The judge does not meter spend, so the ceiling on cost for a v6 errand is not enforced, its rehearsal of the start uses two fresh processes and leaves out checkpoint and restore, and the six older logs were made before the fixes for retries and for overlapping calls.
The pack holds no snapshot of the chain for the dated figures on the price of a seat and on the pay, and nothing that proves which seat is the paid fallback.
about_the_seller: We enter Pocket ourselves, so whoever buys this pack is also our rival there, and we sell it all the same.
The practice judge is our own program, built from the contest's public code and rules, and it is not the contest's own judge, so a pass there is not the contest's verdict.
If the pack turns out not to be what this page says, ask for your money back within seven days of paying, in the way the page on how to buy describes, and it is sent back to the wallet that paid.
pack.paid_in: TAO, at the price of the moment
pack.price_rule: Set on the day the pack went on sale: about half of the entry fee on the day it went on sale, never under $20 and never over $60.

free_trial.what: A free trial of the practice judge runs the rehearsal of the gate and of the production start on your own harness and traces one web task step by step with a scripted model, so it needs no model key and nothing is paid.
free_trial.leaves_out: It gives no score, because it does not run the contest's practice tasks and trust errands with a real model, which is what the pack is for.

contests.name: rec4ll
contests.own_description: Recall is a decentralized RAG and memory API on Bittensor. Miners serve embeddings, reranking, vector search and LLM generation. The Recall API checks their work with continuous verified probes and real customer traffic, and validators set weights from those scores. Developers get encrypted vector databases, search and a free memory MCP for AI coding apps through one simple API.

pack.read_from: rec4ll-main/recall-validator at commit 3c05a47 and rec4ll-main/recall-miner at commit 876b489
holds: An account of how passes become pay, read from the contest's public code: the eight checks and their pass marks, the stages a new seat goes through and the allocation arithmetic, with the file and function named for every statement.

What the chain shows against that code: the pay is an almost equal split among the seats that clear the marks, answer generation is 30% of a full share although the miner's guide calls it optional, and only one hotkey for each coldkey is paid.
Where entries lose: the hours a new seat needs before it is paid in full, set against the protected period, the strict marks of the vector store, and the failures that send a seat back to no pay.

A practice judge that repeats the contest's pay arithmetic exactly, shows when a new seat is first paid and fully paid, and sends stand-in probes to your own embedding, rerank, vector store and generation services before you register.
needs: Python 3.9 or newer and nothing else for pay, ladder, proof and selftest.

For backends, your own miner stack running from the contest's Docker Compose files, because the services are reachable only inside the Compose network; the judge is run inside one of the stack's own containers, which already hold Python.
For backends with the vector store, the stack's own internal key, passed through an environment variable or a file and never on the command line.
For backends with generation, your own account at the generation provider, since every generation probe is a paid request.
For door, a second machine outside your network for the public side, and the certificate file copied from the miner.
cannot_tell: The contest's probes and its rules for a pass are private, so no pass rate measured by the practice judge is the pass rate the contest will measure.
The practice judge has been run against stand-in services only and never against a live miner stack.
How fast is fast enough, how much customer work is credited and how long it takes from paying to the first probe are not public.
about_the_seller: We are not entered in rec4ll ourselves, though we do enter other contests on Bittensor.
The practice judge is our own program, built from the contest's public code and rules, and it is not the contest's own judge, so a pass there is not the contest's verdict.
If the pack turns out not to be what this page says, ask for your money back within seven days of paying, in the way the page on how to buy describes, and it is sent back to the wallet that paid.
pack.price_rule: About half of today's entry fee, never under $20 and never over $60.
pack.not_for_sale_because: its practice judge has only met stand-ins so far, and it goes on sale once it carries numbers from a seat that is really running
